title: Store connected places
summary: A graph stores things and their connections. We can describe school rooms with a dictionary whose lists name directly connected rooms.
introduction: A graph stores things and their connections. We can describe school rooms with a dictionary whose lists name directly connected rooms. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A graph stores things and their connections. We can describe school rooms with a dictionary whose lists name directly connected rooms.
The output is ['class', 'library']. These rooms are one move from the hall. The dictionary does not include travel time.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Add a garden connected to the hall in both directions.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: If travel is allowed both ways, remember to record both connections.
For more detail later, use this [Artificial Intelligence further reading](https://ai4k12.org/resources/).
